title: Exact Values at Special Angles
short: Use 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles to find exact values.
trouble: Students swap sin 30° and sin 60°, writing sin 30° = √3/2.

blocks.html: Most angles have messy sines and cosines. A few have exact values you can find with no calculator, because they come from the two special right triangles. Put each triangle inside the unit circle, with its hypotenuse as a radius of length $1$.

$45^\circ$: the two legs are equal, say $x$. The Pythagorean theorem gives $x^2 + x^2 = 1$, so $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
$30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$: a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle with hypotenuse $1$ is half of an equilateral triangle with sides $1$, so its short side is $\frac{1}{2}$. The other leg is $\sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{4}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. The short side is always across from the small $30^\circ$ angle.

head: $\theta$
$\frac{\pi}{6} = 30^\circ$
$\frac{\pi}{4} = 45^\circ$
$\frac{\pi}{3} = 60^\circ$
$\frac{\pi}{2} = 90^\circ$
blocks.cap: Exact values in the first quadrant. Tangent is $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.

blocks.html: At $30^\circ$ the point on the unit circle is $\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$; at $60^\circ$ it is $\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$; at $45^\circ$ it is $\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$.

blocks.name: unitcircle
blocks.cap: At the special angles the readout shows exact coordinates. Compare $30^\circ$ with $60^\circ$: the coordinates trade places.

blocks.title: A sine
steps: At $60^\circ$ the radius is steep, so the long leg, $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, is the vertical one.

blocks.title: Putting values together
blocks.a: $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ (which is also $\sin 60^\circ$, a hint of things to come)

blocks.html: Swapping $\sin 30^\circ$ and $\sin 60^\circ$, writing $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. Check with the picture: as the angle grows from $0^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, the point climbs, so sine grows. $\sin 30^\circ$ must be the smaller value, $\frac{1}{2}$, and $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.87$ belongs to $60^\circ$.

A memory pattern: $$\sin 0^\circ, \sin 30^\circ, \sin 45^\circ, \sin 60^\circ, \sin 90^\circ$$ are $\frac{\sqrt{0}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{1}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{4}}{2}$. Cosine runs the same list backward.
